items.title: 伯恩斯坦：OpenAI 至 2030 年算力基础设施支出或达 6140 亿美元，低于此前 7500 亿美元传闻
items.description: IT之家 11 月 8 日消息，据智通财经报道，伯恩斯坦分析师 MarkMoerdler 估算，OpenAI 已披露的算力合作协议对应的基础设施支出， 到 2030 年累计可能达到 6,140 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 4.11 万亿元人民币） ， 明显低于《华尔街日报》此前传出的 7,500 亿美元 （现汇率约合 5.02 万亿元人民币） 。 据报道，该测算假设所有已识别合同均按计划执行，但实际支出可能因数据中心建设延期、项目取消及硬件采购安排调整而减少或推迟。由于相关算力通常分批交付，费用也将随设施投运逐步产生，而非立即形成付款义务，预计年度支出将在 2031 年达到 1,840 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1.23 万亿元人民币） 的峰值。 伯恩斯坦指出，OpenAI 与甲骨文、微软和亚马逊的相关协议规模分别约为 3,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 2.01 万亿元人民币） 、2,500 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1.67 万亿元人民币） 和 1,380 亿美元 （现汇率约合 9,233.34 亿元人民币） ，期限通常为五至八年；与 CoreWeave 的协议上限为 224 亿美元

items.description: 北京时间 11 月 8 日，据《WIRED》此前报道及生物科技公司 Exin Therapeutics 最新披露，OpenAI 旗下 AI 模型 GPT-6.1 Sol 已被用于活体小鼠脑部手术实验，并在连续三次操作中，通过外科医生的反馈改善了定位表现。到第三次操作时，其识别关键解剖标志的耗时从 169 秒缩短至 86 秒，定位误差从 0.6 毫米降至 0.3 毫米。 Exin Therapeutics 联合创始人兼 CEO 加布里埃尔 · 奥卡尼亚-桑特罗 (Gabriel Ocana-Santero)11 月 5 日在社交平台 X 上公布了这一结果。研究团队让 GPT-6.1 Sol 连续参与三次活体小鼠脑部手术中的解剖标志定位任务。每次操作结束后，专业外科医生都会纠正 AI 识别的位置，模型则保存相关图像、测量数据及修正记录，供下一次操作参考。 实验主要涉及小鼠头骨表面的两个关键解剖标志：Bregma（前囟点）和 Lambda（后囟点）。这两个位置是脑立体定位手术的重要参考点，研究人员需要借助它们确定脑区坐标，以便将注射针或其他实验器械准确引导至目标位置。 研究团队称， 经过三轮

items.title: Menlo Ventures 报告：中国 AI 模型占全球开源模型企业支出 89%，Kimi、DeepSeek、GLM 位列前三
items.description: IT之家 11 月 8 日消息，据《南华早报》前天报道，一项新研究显示，以月之暗面 Kimi 系列为代表的中国 AI 模型，在全球企业开源模型支出的占比为 89%，接近九成。 IT之家从原报道获悉，硅谷风投公司 Menlo Ventures 近期发布的报告指出上述观点。 其中月之暗面 Kimi 以 61% 份额 ， 在全球企业开源模型支出位居第一 ；深度求索 DeepSeek 以 15% 排名第二；智谱的 GLM 以 11% 位列第三。 相比之下，Meta Platforms 旗下的 Llama 系列是该领域市场份额最高的西方模型，但其在开源模型企业支出中的占比仅为 7%。

items.content: 比如，一个第三方平台声称接入了旗舰模型，后台却换成便宜的小模型、旧模型，光看回答的语气和质量，我们很难判断；又或者是同一道题目，官网能做出来，用中转站却卡住了。 一个看起来简单的模型请求，背后需要经过「用户—中转站—上游服务商—模型」多个环节，只要其中一环缺少透明度，我们就很难确认自己买到的，是不是标价对应的模型。 这套名为 FlashProve 的开源研究原型，可以为模型推理生成密码学证明。它尝试让服务商为模型的计算结果提供密码学证明，用户不用拿到模型权重，也不用自己再跑一遍大模型，就能核验。 除了使用模型厂商官方的应用，和从官网调用 API 进行对话，我们能确认使用模型的情况。在大多数的 API 调用里，我们提交问题，服务器返回回答，模型世界上是跑在了远程的机器上，我们无法得知后台究竟进行了那些计算。 斯坦福大学的研究项目《Model Equality Testing》曾经就测试过 2024 年四款 Llama 模型的 31 个商业 API 端点，发现其中 11 个端点的输出分布，与 Meta 发布权重的参考分布存在统计差异。 同一个模型名字，有时候并不能对应同一种表现。即便在服务页面挂着的都是 Opus 5.5，但根本无法保证用户获得完全相同的模型。

Democrats’ historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could also have a dramatic effect on the tech industry. In dozens of local ballot measures, voters rejected data centers . And even when they weren’t voting on the issue directly, they were electing politicians — like Texas’ new governor-elect Gina Hinojosa — who campaigned on the promise of restricting data centers. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed what the midterms mean for the tech industry. Sean kicked it off by noting that Elon Musk “seems to have basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars” to Republicans, while his companies are now headquartered “in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn.” And Kirsten said that while data centers probably weren’t the main cause of the “blue wave,” they’ve become an “an increasingly grassroots issue, in part because of how hyperscalers and companies have gone about” getting their projects approved. And now, “we’re already seeing companies like OpenAI all of a sudden go, ‘Actually, we can change our policies.’”

items.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
items.description: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo , which was reportedly based on U.S. intelligence. The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed. An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with its customers. A separate NYT report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company authorized by the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced Nvidia chips. But at the office address listed by New Matrix, reporters only found “a hollow gray shell,” raising concerns that it could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm.

items.description: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
items.author: Zack Whittaker
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets. The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities. Microsoft has previously described Artex as a system of AI agents that can conduct cyberattacks “from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with little needed human interaction.” In a blog post , cybersecurity firm Censys, which scans the internet for exposed or vulnerable systems, said that it identified more than 800 distinct deployments of Artex that were accessible from the web without needing a password to log in. Silas Cutler, principal security researcher at Censys who wrote the blog post, said that not every instance of Artex is operated maliciously and many are used for authorized testers

items.description: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it. A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month. As Anthropic gears up for its IPO , the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed. “Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.”

items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Amazon is jumping on the currently most popular bandwagon for interacting with AI agents: texting. The company on Friday said it is launching a feature that lets customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to help them shop, much like you can with AI agents like Muse or Instinct. The move comes after Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse from querying its site in September. The company is rolling the features out just before the start of the holiday shopping season. The e-commerce giant said select U.S. customers will get a text asking them to enable the shopping feature. Those with access can text Alexa to shop on Amazon using natural language queries, spanning everything from searching for items, adding them to cart, and purchasing. The text agent builds on the recent shopping-focused upgrades to Alexa , and so can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products, and check the status of orders. Users can also share a picture of an item or someone wearing an outfit to search for similar listings on Amazon.
